audit_status.source_base: Greek Revelation text tradition with Exodus/Joel/abyss imagery; draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for fifth and sixth trumpets, abyss imagery, locust army symbols, unrepentance.

verses.restored: The fifth messenger trumpeted, and I saw a star fallen from heaven to earth; to him was given the key of the pit of the abyss.

familiar.text: And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit.

modern.text: Then the fifth angel sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to earth, and it was given the key to the pit of the Abyss.

original.text: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ εἶδον ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου·

verses.restored: He opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke went up like smoke of great furnace, and sun and air were darkened from the smoke.

familiar.text: And he opened the bottomless pit; and there arose a smoke out of the pit, as the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by reason of the smoke of the pit.

modern.text: The star opened the pit of the Abyss, and smoke rose out of it like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the pit.

original.text: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου ⸀μεγάλης, καὶ ⸀ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος.

verses.restored: From the smoke locusts came out onto earth, and authority was given them like authority of scorpions of earth.

familiar.text: And there came out of the smoke locusts upon the earth: and unto them was given power, as the scorpions of the earth have power.

modern.text: And out of the smoke, locusts descended on the earth, and they were given power like that of the scorpions of the earth.

original.text: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐταῖς ἐξουσία ὡς ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς.

verses.restored: They were told not to harm grass, green thing, or tree, but only humans without seal of Divine on their foreheads.

familiar.text: And it was commanded them that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree; but only those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads.

modern.text: They were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any plant or tree, but only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads.

original.text: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐταῖς ἵνα μὴ ⸀ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον, εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν ⸀μετώπων.

verses.restored: It was given them not to kill but to torment five months; their torment like torment of scorpion when it strikes a human.

familiar.text: And to them it was given that they should not kill them, but that they should be tormented five months: and their torment was as the torment of a scorpion, when he striketh a man.

modern.text: The locusts were not given power to kill them, but only to torment them for five months, and their torment was like the stinging of a scorpion.

original.text: καὶ ἐδόθη ⸀αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα ⸀βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε· καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου, ὅταν παίσῃ ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: In those days humans will seek death and not find it; they will desire to die, and death flees from them.

familiar.text: And in those days shall men seek death, and shall not find it; and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them.

modern.text: In those days men will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, but death will escape them.

original.text: καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνατον καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρήσουσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐπιθυμήσουσιν ἀποθανεῖν καὶ ⸀φεύγει ⸂ὁ θάνατος ἀπʼ αὐτῶν⸃.

verses.restored: The likenesses of locusts were like horses prepared for war; on heads like crowns of gold, faces like human faces.

familiar.text: And the shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared unto battle; and on their heads were as it were crowns like gold, and their faces were as the faces of men.

modern.text: And the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle, with something like crowns of gold on their heads, and faces like the faces of men.

original.text: Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι ⸂ὅμοιοι χρυσῷ⸃, καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων,

verses.restored: They had hair like women's hair, and teeth like lions' teeth.

familiar.text: And they had hair as the hair of women, and their teeth were as the teeth of lions.

modern.text: They had hair like that of women, and teeth like those of lions.

original.text: καὶ εἶχον τρίχας ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν,

verses.restored: They had breastplates like iron, and sound of wings like sound of many chariots with horses running into battle.

familiar.text: And they had breastplates, as it were breastplates of iron; and the sound of their wings was as the sound of chariots of many horses running to battle.

modern.text: They also had thoraxes like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.

original.text: καὶ εἶχον θώρακας ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον·

verses.restored: They have tails like scorpions and stings; in their tails is authority to harm humans five months.

familiar.text: And they had tails like unto scorpions, and there were stings in their tails: and their power was to hurt men five months.

modern.text: They had tails with stingers like scorpions, which had the power to injure people for five months.

original.text: καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα, καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ⸂ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν⸃ ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε.

verses.restored: They have over them king, messenger of abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has name Apollyon.

familiar.text: And they had a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in the Hebrew tongue is Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath his name Apollyon.

modern.text: They were ruled by a king, the angel of the Abyss. His name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek it is Apollyon.

original.text: ⸂ἔχουσιν ἐπʼ αὐτῶν βασιλέα τὸν⸃ ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου· ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών, ⸂καὶ ἐν⸃ τῇ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει Ἀπολλύων.

verses.restored: The first woe went away; look, two woes still come after these.

familiar.text: One woe is past; and, behold, there come two woes more hereafter.

modern.text: The first woe has passed. Behold, two woes are still to follow. The Sixth Trumpet

original.text: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ μία ἀπῆλθεν· ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο οὐαὶ μετὰ ταῦτα.

verses.restored: The sixth messenger trumpeted, and I heard one voice from four horns of golden altar before the Divine,

familiar.text: And the sixth angel sounded, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God,

modern.text: Then the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God

original.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ ⸀τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: saying to the sixth messenger with trumpet: Release the four messengers bound at the great river Euphrates.

familiar.text: Saying to the sixth angel which had the trumpet, Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates.

modern.text: saying to the sixth angel with the trumpet, “Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.”

original.text: ⸀λέγοντα τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀγγέλῳ, ὁ ἔχων τὴν σάλπιγγα· Λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ.

verses.restored: And the four messengers were released, prepared for hour, day, month, and year, so that a third of humans might be killed.

familiar.text: And the four angels were loosed, which were prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, for to slay the third part of men.

modern.text: So the four angels who had been prepared for this hour and day and month and year were released to kill a third of mankind.

original.text: καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν ⸀καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: Number of armies of horsemen was two myriads of myriads; I heard their number.

familiar.text: And the number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand: and I heard the number of them.

modern.text: And the number of mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number.

original.text: καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ⸀ἱππικοῦ ⸀δισμυριάδες μυριάδων· ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: And thus I saw horses in the vision and those sitting on them, having breastplates fire-colored, hyacinth, and sulfur-like; heads of horses like heads of lions, and from their mouths come fire, smoke, and sulfur.

familiar.text: And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and them that sat on them, having breastplates of fire, and of jacinth, and brimstone: and the heads of the horses were as the heads of lions; and out of their mouths issued fire and smoke and brimstone.

modern.text: Now the horses and riders in my vision looked like this: The riders had breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire, and sulfur. The heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths proceeded fire, smoke, and sulfur.

original.text: καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπʼ αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις· καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων, καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον.

verses.restored: By these three plagues a third of humans were killed: from fire, smoke, and sulfur coming from their mouths.

familiar.text: By these three was the third part of men killed, by the fire, and by the smoke, and by the brimstone, which issued out of their mouths.

modern.text: A third of mankind was killed by the three plagues of fire, smoke, and sulfur that proceeded from their mouths.

original.text: ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ⸀ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: For authority of horses is in their mouths and tails; their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with them they harm.

familiar.text: For their power is in their mouth, and in their tails: for their tails were like unto serpents, and had heads, and with them they do hurt.

modern.text: For the power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails; indeed, their tails were like snakes, having heads with which to inflict harm.

original.text: ἡ γὰρ ἐξουσία τῶν ἵππων ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν· αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ⸀ὄφεσιν, ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς, καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν.

verses.restored: The rest of humans, who were not killed by these plagues, did not turn from works of their hands, so as not to worship daimons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk.

familiar.text: And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: which neither can see, nor hear, nor walk:

modern.text: Now the rest of mankind who were not killed by these plagues still did not repent of the works of their hands. They did not stop worshiping demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which cannot see or hear or walk.

original.text: Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἳ οὐκ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν ταῖς πληγαῖς ταύταις, ⸀οὐδὲ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ ⸀προσκυνήσουσιν τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ χρυσᾶ καὶ τὰ ἀργυρᾶ καὶ τὰ χαλκᾶ καὶ τὰ λίθινα καὶ τὰ ξύλινα, ἃ οὔτε βλέπειν ⸀δύνανται οὔτε ἀκούειν οὔτε περιπατεῖν,

verses.restored: And they did not turn from murders, sorceries, sexual misuses, nor thefts.

familiar.text: Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

modern.text: Furthermore, they did not repent of their murder, sorcery, sexual immorality, and theft.

original.text: καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν φόνων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν ⸀φαρμάκων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν.

translation_notes: Abyss/locust imagery is symbolic plague/anti-creation imagery; avoid literal monster speculation.
The chapter's moral endpoint is unrepentant idolatry and works of hands.
safety_note: Do not use Revelation 9 to incite fear, self-harm, or target people. Treat the images as symbolic exposure of destructive powers and idolatrous systems.
